title: Friday Northern Lights Forecast: 10 States May See The Aurora Borealis
excerpt: Much of the northern U.S. border will see mild auroral activity.
content:
Topline

The aurora borealis may be seen in up to 11 states Friday night, according to a forecast from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, which predicts mild auroral activity.

Key Facts

NOAA issued a Kp index of five for Friday night, which means the aurora may be "quite pleasing" to look at for observers in the right areas.

No geomagnetic storm impacts, which tend to strengthen northern lights showings, are forecast for Friday night.

Northern lights visibility will lessen by Saturday night, when the Kp index is forecast to fall to four.

Where Will The Northern Lights Be Visible?

The northern lights have a low chance of visibility in areas including northern Washington, the northern tip of Idaho, northern Montana, the northern edge of Wyoming, North Dakota, South Dakota along its northern border, northern Minnesota, northern Wisconsin, the Upper Peninsula of Michigan and the northern tip of Michigan. Alaska will have the best chance of seeing the northern lights, with visibility generally improving the farther inland observers are.

What's The Best Way To See The Northern Lights?

Viewing the northern lights from high vantage points and places with little to no light pollution can improve visibility. The ideal time to try and catch a look at the aurora is between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m.

What's The Best Way To Photograph The Northern Lights?

Traditional cameras should use wide-angle lenses, tripods and low apertures when shooting the northern lights. Smartphone users can use night mode and should avoid using flash.

Key Background

The northern lights, which are formed when charged particles from the sun interact with gas in Earth's atmosphere, are usually seen as a green color. Auroral activity reached a 500-year high in 2024 as the sun reached the peak of its 11-year solar cycle. The more time passes from that peak, the less auroral activity will be registered.
